intent: Decision: who trains (one-off Job vs first pod) and training traffic
Record ADR 0002: Job-per-fingerprint trainer and training traffic

title: chose a Helm-hook Job named by fingerprint over first-pod training
why: The Kubernetes Job name is unique per namespace, so a fingerprint-named Job de-duplicates concurrent trainers without a lock, and serving pods need no Job-create permission.
alternative: Init container creates the Job — rejected: gives every app pod Job-create RBAC

title: chose spring-refresh default with http-probe opt-in; deferred user warmup script
why: Both modes already exist in the training runner; a warmup script would run arbitrary code with cluster secrets.
alternative: User warmup script in v0.2.0 — rejected: security and secrets exposure

name: Training Job
role: Per-fingerprint Job that checks the store, trains if missing, uploads, and exits
conditions: Must be idempotent: exit 0 when the fingerprint already exists

subject: Clean exit writes the archive
why: The JVM dumps the archive only on a clean exit, so a serving pod cannot double as the trainer

subject: Pods starting before training finishes
why: They run uncached by design (constitution §1); the next rollout benefits
